audit_scope: ROUND-2 adversarial meta-audit of the round-2 real-entity repair (Elin Sarauw -> Adela Rowsholme; Marta Vey -> Frances Talvenny), following this file's round-1 REFUTED verdict. generator_meta.originality_note was taken apart claim by claim and every factual assertion in it was independently reproduced (or found unreproducible). Every named entity in the CURRENT passage was re-verified from scratch through five independent channels, including three exact-match indices the note itself says it did not use.

findings.claim: Every testable assertion in the round-2 originality_note reproduces. Nothing in it was certified without being run.
findings.evidence: TOOLING PREAMBLE: reproduced exactly. My first WebSearch call returned 'this session has used its web search budget (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)'; mcp firecrawl_search returned 'Request failed with status code 401' and firecrawl_scrape 'Unauthorized: Invalid token'. The note's disclosure that all its queries ran on a semantic engine, and that this is weaker than an exact-phrase nil, is honest and correct. (1) Elin Sarauw: reproduced verbatim by direct page fetch of goteborgsstadsmuseum.se/en/online/vardefullt/various-worths/sentimental-value/ — 'They were worn by Elin Sarauw, who was born in 1886. She was married to Georg Sarauw, who became the head of a new archaeology department at Gothenburg Museum in 1912.' (2) Marta Vey: reproduced — dunailline.org/2019/09/21/druidas-salvajes-en-el-vii-dia-del-paganisme-conferencia-de-marta-vey/, author byline 'de Marta Vey', body 'Marta Vey, Archidruidesa de HDDA', 'Transcripcion de la conferencia realizada el 21 de septiembre de 2019 por Marta Vey'; plus dunailline.org/author/dunailline/ and a 2013 conference notice 'Sra. Dna. Marta Vey. Seanoir de la Hermandad Druida Dun Ailline'. Both withdrawals in the note are therefore correctly grounded. (3) Rejected-candidate screening spot-checked: 'Pelverin' reproduces exactly — popular-pharma.com/products/pelverin, 'Pelverin / Alverine Citrate / 60 mg', Popular Pharmaceuticals Ltd, Dhaka; corroborated by medsbd.com and medeasy.health. (4)/(5) 'Talvenny' and 'Rowsholme': no exact-string bearer surfaced on my own Exa queries; returns were near-neighbours only (Talvainn, Talvyn, Talvin, Talvany, Talvan, Talvanen, Talwani / Rusholme, Rowsome, Rowsell, Rowswell, Newsholme). Query 'Adela Rowsholme essayist writer' returned exactly the four unrelated Adelas the note names (Castell, Zamudio, Sloss-Vento, Pineda Franco). (6) 'Wenmarch': no company, place or person; returns were Wen-/March- fragments only. (7) 'Ferrowby': the cited real bearer reproduces verbatim by direct fetch of mkheritage.org.uk/wsc/the-dukes-head-aspley-guise/ — 'one, a labourer, Frederick Ferrowby, was lodging there at the time that he had an accident at work and fell from 40 feet, breaking three ribs and his arm ... in April 1891'; the volunteered fictional-namesake disclosure also reproduces verbatim on jonsparksauthor.com/whos-who.html — 'Ferrowby: in VAW, Hedric's cousin and rival for the inheritance of Skilthorn.' (8) 'Uniform Papers Committee': no body of that name; the real 1911 event is confirmed as Wilhelm Ostwald's root-two Weltformat via Die Bruecke, with DIN 476 published 18 Aug 1922 by Walter Porstmann and Lichtenberg's 1786 letter as ancestor — exactly as stated, and none of those is named in the passage. English Wikipedia full-text search for the quoted phrase 'Uniform Papers Committee' returns totalhits 0. (9) Bank registry reproduced by my own grep over batches/*/candidates-final/*.json: Talvenny, Rowsholme, Frances, Adela, Wenmarch, Crispin and Ferrowby each hit exactly one file, this one. The 'avoid-list' the note invokes is GENERATION.md section 13 (saturated 'Hal-' prefix and 'Ingrid', plus no reuse of any shipped full name/surname/institute/toponym); neither replacement violates it. (10) Field-change claim independently re-derived by programmatic diff against HEAD (see the dedicated finding below): keys, option letters, option order, option texts, prompts and passage all behave exactly as claimed.
findings.why: The round-1 failure mode was a note that sounded thorough and had not been run. This note is the opposite: it labels its own tooling limitation, withdraws its predecessor's two false claims by name, cites hits it can be checked against, and volunteers a finding (the Jon Sparks namesake) that no auditor had raised. Every item I could test reproduced; none failed.

findings.stage_challenged: real-entity-repair (independent exact-match verification beyond the note)
findings.claim: The note's own disclosed residual risk — that Talvenny and Rowsholme were screened only by a semantic engine and never against a registry or authority index — was closed by this audit against four exact-match indices, all with a working positive control. No real bearer exists in any domain the passage inhabits.
findings.evidence: All four names in the current passage's entity set were queried against exact-match indices via direct HTTP: (a) English Wikipedia search API — Talvenny totalhits 0, Rowsholme 0 (suggests 'rusholme'), Wenmarch 0 (suggests 'wwe march'), Ferrowby 0 (suggests 'ferriby'). (b) Wikidata wbsearchentities — empty result set for all four. (c) Crossref works?query.author — total-results 0 for all four; POSITIVE CONTROL 'Porstmann' returns 206. (d) UK Companies House public search (find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/search) — 'No results found' for Wenmarch, Talvenny, Rowsholme and Ferrowby, covering both companies and officers in the jurisdiction the passage implies for an 'Assurance Office'. Wikidata POSITIVE CONTROL 'Porstmann' returns 'Walter Porstmann, German mathematician (1886-1959)'. Channels that could not be used and are therefore not claimed: DuckDuckGo lite (bot challenge), Mojeek (automated-query block), forebears.io (Cloudflare interstitial), VIAF AutoSuggest (returns HTML for the control too), Open Library (503).
findings.why: This is the evidence class the round-1 failure lacked and the round-2 note honestly said it could not supply. Crossref and Wikidata rule out a published author or notable person of any of these names; Companies House rules out a UK corporate bearer of 'Wenmarch'. The passage's risk surface is authors, design writers, historians, standards bodies and assurance firms, and all four are now nil on indices that match strings rather than meanings.

findings.stage_challenged: real-entity-repair (defect closure + mechanical diff, re-derived not accepted)
findings.claim: The defect this unit was refuted for is genuinely gone, and the repair changed nothing it was not supposed to change.
findings.evidence: OLD NAMES PURGED: parsing the JSON and excising generator_meta.originality_note leaves 0 occurrences of 'Sarauw', 'Elin', 'Marta', 'Vey', 'Halloran', 'Piet' and 'Northern' anywhere in the file; the 23 raw grep hits are all inside the note that documents the fix. The passage's exhaustive capitalised-entity set is now {Uniform Papers Committee, Frances Talvenny, Wenmarch Assurance Office, Crispin Ferrowby, Adela Rowsholme} — no toponym, no publication title. DIFF vs HEAD, computed here rather than trusted: keys are C,B,D,A,B in both. Reconstructing HEAD with the four renames applied reproduces the current passage byte-for-byte and all five rationales byte-for-byte. Prompts differ from HEAD only at q3 ('Northern'->'Wenmarch') and q5 ('Halloran'->'Ferrowby'); option text differs only at q4/B ('Northern'->'Wenmarch') — all three are round-1 edits, so the round-2 claim that prompts and option texts were byte-identical across THIS round holds (no prompt or option in the pre-round-2 file contained 'Vey' or 'Sarauw'; verified by counting those substrings field by field on HEAD). generator_meta diffs vs HEAD are confined to fictional_source, fictional_entities, engineered_traps, stance_item_fix and originality_note, and only the first two plus the note carry round-2 names. CONSISTENCY PROBE: q5's key B says 'she grants the geometry was necessary' — 'she' resolves to the byline, which was female (Elin) and remains female (Adela), so the rename did not break pronoun agreement; q5's rationale 'the writer answers through Talvenny' matches the passage's 'Talvenny is more careful'; Q3's numbers (fewer than thirty / passed six hundred / four years / 1911 rule / 1913 order) reconcile with the passage. Independent re-run of gates/scripts/run_mech.py --no-plagiarism: M-SCHEMA, M-BANDS, M-TELL, M-FORM all pass, confirming the 4/4 recorded in reviews/pedagogy.jsonl. Fresh entityfix-r2 lines are the LAST records for this unit in verdicts-gdistractor.jsonl (26-30), verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl (26-30), verdicts-gkey-2.jsonl (26-30) and verdicts-gstem.jsonl (11-15).
findings.why: Refutation is lifted only if the specific defect is closed and the closure cost nothing else. Both hold.

findings.claim: The note's 'passage (the six name tokens only)' undercounts. The round-2 rename touched five sites and seven tokens, not six.
findings.evidence: In the pre-round-2 passage: 'Marta' x1, 'Vey' x4 (one of them inside 'Marta Vey', three bare), 'Elin' x1, 'Sarauw' x1. That is five substitution sites ('Marta Vey' x1, bare 'Vey' x3, 'Elin Sarauw' x1) and seven word tokens. The current passage correspondingly carries 'Frances' x1, 'Talvenny' x4, 'Adela' x1, 'Rowsholme' x1. 'Six' matches neither count.
findings.why: The substantive half of the claim — that the passage differs from the pre-edit file ONLY at renamed tokens — I re-derived myself and it is true. Only the parenthetical count is wrong. Recorded because a note whose whole purpose is to be checkable should not carry a number that fails the check, but this is a slip in a description, not a certified check that was never run.

findings.claim: The entityfix-r2 G-DISTRACTOR regate returned a NEW major-severity flag on q:4 that both earlier generations passed, and reviews/final_verify.jsonl still records 'gdistr_flags=0' for this unit and was not re-run.
findings.evidence: verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gdistractor.jsonl line 29: '"verdict": "flag"', severity major, on q4 option B ('That the Wenmarch Assurance Office had ordered all of its own correspondence to be kept and filed on the folding size'), executed_by 'claude-opus-4-8/G-DISTRACTOR-entityfix-r2'. Lines 9-10 (original G-DISTRACTOR) and 21-25 (entityfix r1) are all 'pass' with empty findings. reviews/final_verify.jsonl line 2 for elf-b7-002 reads 'gkey_records=10 gkey_kills=0 gdistr_kills=0 gdistr_flags=0 audit=CONFIRMED_NOTES audit_major=0 audit_minor=1', date 2026-07-24, and is the only final_verify record for the unit. verdicts-gstem.jsonl line 9 independently flags the same option.
findings.why: The flag itself is adjudicated inside its own note ('Key support is clearly stronger than the distractor case') and I agree on the merits — q4's stem carries two delimiters ('among ordinary firms', 'once the Assurance Office had adopted it') that B cannot satisfy, so B is not defensible as a second key. But the unit's shipped verify record now asserts facts about the unit ('gdistr_flags=0', 'audit=CONFIRMED_NOTES') that its own latest gate and its own audit file both contradict. That is a provenance inconsistency, not a content defect.

findings.claim: The upstream adjudication record that produced the wrong keep still carries the falsified assertion, uncorrected.
findings.evidence: adjudication/real-entity/verdicts-b7-8.json line 54ff: '"name": "Elin Sarauw"' with '"evidence": "No bearer found; Sarauw is a rare Scandinavian surname with no figure in this or an adjacent domain."' adjudication/real-entity/entities-b7-8.json lines 31 and 46 still list 'Marta Vey' and 'Elin Sarauw'.

Recorded because the same false 'No bearer found' evidence string is the artefact that let the name ship in the first place, and a future sweep that trusts this file will repeat the error.

findings.claim: Three fragments presented in quotation marks inside the rationales are not verbatim against the current passage or options. Pre-existing, untouched by either rename round.
findings.evidence: Of 29 quoted fragments of >=8 characters across the five rationales, 26 resolve verbatim against the passage or option text. The three that do not: q1 'This is not how ... the maths was always going to win' — the passage has 'This is not how the design press likes to tell it' and, separately, 'The maths was always going to win' with a capital T, so the ellipsis silently crosses a sentence boundary and lowercases the resumption; q4 'publicised the geometric advantages' — option C reads 'publicised the folding proportion's geometric advantages'; q5 'poor choice ... forced on an unwilling trade' — option D reads 'a poor choice that a single office ended up forcing on an unwilling and resistant trade'. (A fourth non-match, q5's 'pick the only hedged option among absolutes', is a description of a solver heuristic, not a quotation, and is correctly not verbatim.)
findings.why: These are teaching-payload citations that a student may check against the text. All three are loose rather than wrong in substance, none affects a key, and none was introduced by the entity repair — but the round-1 audit's 'all 22 passage fragments occur verbatim' was scoped to passage quotes and did not cover the option quotes, so this is recorded rather than left implicit.

findings.claim: Carried forward from both prior audits and re-verified as still true: Q4 is labelled ELF-TYPE-002 (inference) but the keyed option A is a near-verbatim restatement of the passage.
findings.evidence: Passage: 'a firm that bought those cabinets found the folding sheet was the sheet that fitted the drawer.' Option A (key): 'a firm buying cabinets found the folding sheet was the one that fitted its drawers.'
findings.why: Label-generosity only; the item still discriminates on the intended spread-mechanism axis because distractor B is also a passage echo. Unaffected by either rename round.

findings.claim: The round-2 rename preserved the careful-woman-researcher / overconfident-man-challenger configuration that GENERATION.md section 13 names as saturated across the bank.
findings.evidence: GENERATION.md lines 156-162: 'Randomise researcher and challenger gender independently (the scan found careful-woman/overconfident-man 18 of 18)'. This unit: careful archival historian Frances Talvenny (female), overconfident design writer Crispin Ferrowby (male) — the same configuration as the pre-repair Marta Vey / Piet Halloran pairing.
findings.why: Not a regression and not in scope for an entity repair: the passage's third-person references to Talvenny and to the byline writer would all have had to change, and the repair correctly kept its blast radius minimal. Recorded only so that the configuration is not later mistaken for a randomised outcome.
